## About

Krishal Karna is a backend and applied ML engineer based in Bangalore, India
— a final-year B.E. Computer Science & Engineering student at Jain
(Deemed-to-be) University, Bangalore, graduating in June 2027 with a CGPA of
9.5/10 (top 1% of batch). He is an EdCIL COMPEX Scholar — a Government of
India merit scholarship covering full tuition. He builds Django and Django
REST Framework backends, scikit-learn ML pipelines, LangGraph LLM systems,
and n8n automations — most recently DataLens AI, a full-stack data quality
platform — along with the Next.js frontends that make them usable. He is
open to backend engineering, applied ML, and AI engineering roles for the
2027 graduating batch.

## How I Got Here

Java + DSA + Spring Boot (year 1) -> scikit-learn & applied ML (year 2) ->
FastAPI model serving (year 3) -> Django + DRF (now).

Krishal started backend-heavy in Java, got pulled into machine learning in
his second year, and learned to serve models as APIs with FastAPI. He has
since moved to Django and DRF for production apps, where the model is one
component of a real product rather than the whole demo.

Going deeper right now: multi-agent LangGraph workflows, RAG and retrieval
pipelines, model serving at scale, Django internals and query optimization.

## Featured Projects

### DataLens AI
Live: https://dataquality-ai.vercel.app/
Repo: https://github.com/kreeshal17/Datalens-AI
Stack: Django REST, Next.js, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, scikit-learn, LangGraph, Gemini, Docker, AWS EC2

Full-stack data quality platform that ingests CSV datasets, profiles row- and
column-level statistics, and computes an overall quality score. The ML
pipeline uses Isolation Forest for anomaly detection, KNN imputation for
missing values, and TF-IDF + cosine similarity for near-duplicate detection.
LLM-driven root cause analysis built with LangGraph and Google Gemini
explains why each quality issue occurred. JWT auth, Dockerized backend on
AWS EC2 behind Gunicorn, Postgres on Neon, frontend on Vercel.

Problem: "Is this dataset any good?" is normally answered by hand.
Approach: Automated profiling plus three ML passes, with an LLM layer explaining causes in structured output.
Result: Upload a CSV, get a scored, diagnosed, explained quality verdict.

Under the hood:
- Profiling — row- and column-level statistics (type inference, null density, cardinality, distribution shape) rolled into a single quality score trackable across uploads.
- The scikit-learn pass:
  - Isolation Forest -> Which rows don't belong?
  - KNN imputation -> What should the missing values have been?
  - TF-IDF + cosine similarity -> Which rows are near-duplicates of each other?
- Root cause — a LangGraph + Gemini layer converts raw findings into plain-language explanations plus structured fix recommendations under an enforced schema, so the frontend renders them instead of parsing prose.
- Shipping it — Docker + Gunicorn on EC2, managed Postgres, frontend on Vercel. ML runs inside the request cycle, so latency was a design constraint rather than an afterthought.

### Luma AI Studio
Live: https://codewithluma.vercel.app/
Repo: https://github.com/kreeshal17/LUMA-AI-STUDIO
Stack: Next.js, FastAPI, LangGraph, Gemini, PostgreSQL

Full-stack AI coding agent generating/editing React components from natural
language. LangGraph tool-calling loop backed by Gemini, live Sandpack
preview, persistent multi-turn sessions, GitHub OAuth repo push, deployed on
Vercel + Railway.

Problem: Generating a React component from a prompt is the easy half; the hard half is the second prompt — "now make the sidebar collapsible" — without regenerating and breaking everything else.
Approach: Component-driven architecture where each generation is a diff against persisted session state rather than a fresh render, with a live Sandpack preview and session history in Postgres.
Result: Multi-turn incremental editing with GitHub OAuth push straight to a repo.

### BookMandu
Live: https://bookmandu.vercel.app/
Repo: https://github.com/kreeshal17/bookbazaar
Stack: Next.js, Prisma, PostgreSQL, Tailwind, Vercel AI SDK

Multi-vendor book marketplace: seller onboarding with identity verification,
real-time stock management, delivery-gated review system, AI chat assistant,
JWT auth, Redis caching, Cloudinary-backed listings, custom domain.

Problem: A review from someone who never bought the book is worth nothing, but most marketplaces let anyone post one anyway.
Approach: A delivery-gated review system — only verified buyers who actually received the book can leave a review — that's a trust-design decision, not a CRUD feature.
Result: A multi-vendor marketplace where reviews mean something, backed by seller onboarding, real-time stock, and an AI chat assistant.

### Production-Grade Retail SQL Analytics
Repo: https://github.com/kreeshal17/production-grade-sql-analytics
Stack: SQL, Statistics, A/B Testing, CTEs

Analyzed 1M+ sales records using CTEs, window functions, A/B testing and
t-tests at 95% CI, surfaced pricing optimizations driving 6–9% statistically
significant sales uplift.

Problem: Whether a pricing change actually worked is normally answered by gut feel, not statistics.
Approach: CTEs, window functions, and A/B testing with t-tests at 95% confidence over 1M+ retail sales records.
Result: Pricing optimizations with a statistically significant 6–9% sales uplift.
